comments.text:
I went to India and most places didn't look this bad.   In poor areas though like Old Delhi is was pretty rough.  Busy street intersections like in Agra are just gridlock.  You see some bad poverty in some places like people bathing in broken water mains.  Surprisingly getting out into rural areas isn't as bad.

I was nervous for the women I was traveling with if they wanted to walk around by themselves I said I wanted to look around with them but I was partially going to be a bodyguard.

Crossing a busy road is comparable to crossing a stream.  You wait for a gap then slowly, and steadily, walk across.  The key is to be predictable and constant and they will weave around you.

Britain colonized India for 200 years, spanning from the mid-18th century until 1947. Under British rule, Britain drained India's wealth, siphoning Indian resources to Britain without any commercial or material return. 

Economist Utsa Patnaik estimated that Britain siphoned off nearly $45 trillion (in modern value) between 1765 and 1938, starving India of the internal capital required for its own industrial modernization. 

Investments in public education, healthcare, and advanced domestic tech industries were kept intentionally minimal. By the time the British departed in 1947, India's literacy rate stood at a mere 12%.
